title: Per-token latency attribution and cache-impact correlation for billing & SLO debugging
creator: Riley Zhang
description:
Motivation: We need fine-grained attribution that ties per-request cost and latency regressions to the exact emission path. Current request-level metrics mask token-level variability introduced by prefix cache hits, cold KV loads, and async kernel scheduling. This ticket implements a lightweight per-token timing shim and cache-impact correlation pipeline that answers questions such as: which tokens incur extra latency due to KV misses, how much tail latency is attributable to kernel contention vs cache warming, and how to map those costs back to billing/chargeback and SLO diagnostics.

Scope: Instrument runtime entry points to emit compact token events (arrival_ts, emit_ts, cache_tag, request_id, model_variant) without adding backpressure to the fast path. Add enrichers in our pipeline to correlate token events with trace ids and cache hit/miss metadata. Produce an aggregated view and a set of dashboard panels for: (1) per-token median/p95 by position in sequence, (2) cache-hit vs cache-miss latency delta, (3) contributor breakdown (KV lookup, kernel schedule, network), and (4) request-level chargeback rollup.

Non-goals: This is not a wholesale billing rewrite or a full per-subtoken billing ledger. We will not change pricing in this ticket; focus is observability and internal chargeback reconciliation for SRE and product troubleshooting.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits compact token events at <=2 microseconds added overhead in hot path (measured by microbench)
Event schema includes request_id, token_index, emit_latency_us, cache_status, model_variant, and sampling_flag
Streaming pipeline enriches token events with trace ids and KV cache metrics and writes to the telemetry lake within ingestion SLA
Dashboard panels for token-level median/p95 by token index and cache status exist in Grafana with documented queries
End-to-end tests that simulate cache-hit and cache-miss scenarios produce expected delta distributions and are stable in CI
tasks: Design compact token event schema and sampling strategy (schema doc + examples)
Add tracing hook in serving runtime to emit token events with cache_status tag
Implement non-blocking emitter backed by bounded ring buffer to avoid client latency impact
Extend ingestion transform to join token events with KV cache telemetry from runtime logs
Build aggregation job: per-request rollup and per-token position histograms (hourly)
Create Grafana dashboard with panels and runbook links
Add deterministic unit and integration tests that exercise cache hit/miss and quantize timings
Prepare rollout plan with 1% -> 10% -> 100% sampling gates and monitor overhead metrics
Write docs for SDK consumers and internal SRE runbook
comments: 2025-01-15: Ticket created — initial proposal to address noisy tail latencies suspected to be KV misses (Riley Zhang)
2025-01-21: Design review — agreed to use a sampled emit strategy with deterministic seed tied to request_id to ensure reproducible sampling (Aisha K.)
2025-01-27: Prototype benchmark — ring buffer emitter adds ~1.6us median overhead on hot path, p99 at 3.8us. Need to trim payload fields for release (Tomás M.)
2025-01-30: PM review — product asked for per-customer rollups for internal chargeback; adding aggregate tag to rollup to avoid leaking PII (Eleni P.)
2025-02-02: Infra note — ingestion job requires extra partitioning to avoid hotspotting when correlating with KV logs; infra will add secondary index (SRE team)
2025-02-04: Implementation in progress — added schema and tracing hook PR opened (PR:github.com/redwood/serving/pull/4987); running integration against staging telemetry pipeline (Aisha K.)
notes: Tradeoffs discussed: keep event schema tiny to limit egress and CPU cost vs. richer context for faster debugging. Decided on two-level approach: compact event emitted everywhere + full debug trace when sampled. Will revisit schema v2 if signal is insufficient.
